rows.R: Main p1 abstract (6 of 7 secondary outcomes not significant, incl. QoL) and p6 ('no differences in quality of life', citing eTables 2-4) vs supp3 eTable 3 p4: day-7 EQ-5D index -0.057 (-0.104 to -0.010), P=.02 favoring control; CI-implied P=0.017. SAP p26 names day 7 as a primary QoL time point and p12 uses alpha .05 without multiplicity correction. Interaction P=.10 does not remove the day-specific result. Card agrees.
rows.evidence: jama_atherton...pdf pp1,4,6,8 (text); joi240145supp3 pp3-4 (text); joi240145supp1 SAP pp12,26 (text). Card C001 read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The abstract counts quality of life among the secondary outcomes without significant difference and the body states 'There were no differences in quality of life between the 2 groups (eTables 2-4)'. eTable 3 prints a day-7 EQ-5D index adjusted mean difference of -0.057 (95% CI -0.104 to -0.010), P=.02, i.e., worse quality of life with iNPWT. Recomputed P from the CI: se=(0.094)/3.92=0.024, z=2.38, P=0.0175, consistent with the printed .02. The SAP (p26) defines day 7 and day 30 as primary time points for the QoL contrasts from the treatment x time model and (p12) tests at two-sided 5% without multiplicity correction, so the day-7 contrast is a prespecified test that the summary statements contradict. The nonsignificant interaction (P=.10) tests a different null. The MCS day-7 contrast (P=.06) is borderline but not significant. Issue confirmed as a contradiction between the narrative/abstract and the cited result; substantive because the abstract-level summary omits a significant adverse secondary-outcome contrast. Downstream: possible (QoL extraction from abstract).

rows.R: SAP p25/p42: LOS analysed UK-only by linear mixed model as adjusted mean difference (days); protocol p39: if skewed, unadjusted median difference. Report p4/p6/p8: log-transformed, ratio of geometric means, for UK and also pooled UK+Australia (pooled result in abstract); no additive difference reported. Partly disclosed (skewness stated, p4); SAP p15 allows transformation only as a sensitivity analysis.
rows.evidence: joi240145supp1 SAP pp15,25,42; joi240145supp4 protocol pp24,39; jama_atherton pp1,4,6,8 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The SAP specifies a UK-only mixed-effects linear regression giving an adjusted mean difference with 95% CI (p25; shell p42 'Adjusted mean difference'); SAP 9.2 (p15) says the proposed primary method is followed first and transformation is examined as sensitivity analysis. The protocol (p39) specifies adjusted mean difference or, if skewed, an unadjusted difference between medians, and p24 restricts LOS to UK patients. The report presents adjusted ratios of geometric means after log transformation (Table 3 footnote c) for UK patients and additionally for pooled UK and Australian patients, and the pooled ratio is the one in the abstract. Neither planned estimand (additive mean difference or median difference) is reported. This is a change of effect measure and of the foregrounded population. Disclosed in part (non-normality explained, p4). L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Main p2 lists 'not expected to survive beyond 30 days' as an exclusion and p10 invokes it; protocol v4.0 §5.2 p17 and summary p8 list only two exclusions (abdominal surgery within 3 months; expected return to theatre). CONSORT ineligibility reasons (p5) also lack a survival category. Earlier protocol versions not supplied; v4.0 is the latest.
rows.evidence: jama_atherton pp2,5 (Figure 1 footnote),10 (text); joi240145supp4 protocol pp2,8,17 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The report's eligibility paragraph adds a third exclusion, 'were not expected to survive beyond 30 days', and the discussion explains low mortality by noting that patients unlikely to survive 30 days were not included. The supplied protocol (v4.0, 16 Mar 2021, the final amendment before recruitment ended) lists only two exclusions and its amendment log does not mention a survival restriction. The inclusion criterion 'willing and able to undergo follow-up at 30 days' is not the same criterion. The CONSORT footnote's ineligibility reasons contain no survival category, so how the stated criterion was applied is unclear. Population definition differs between plan and report; recorded as a substantive difference in the eligibility definition (descriptive only). Separately, Table 1 lists 7 ASA class V patients, which sits uneasily with the discussion's example of excluded patients (ASA 5).

rows.R: SAP §9.6 p26: repeated-measures mixed model with unstructured covariance and robust sandwich SEs for SF-12, inherited by EQ-5D index and health. Main p4: 'an independent covariance structure was assumed'. Not disclosed as a change. Affects all QoL contrasts in Table 3 and eTables 2-4.
rows.evidence: joi240145supp1 SAP p26; jama_atherton p4, p8; joi240145supp3 pp3-4 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The two documents make positive and incompatible statements about the within-participant covariance structure of the same longitudinal QoL models (unstructured vs independent). An independent structure ignores within-participant correlation unless paired with robust SEs, which the report does not mention. This is a change in analysis model for all SF-12 and EQ-5D contrasts. Not labeled as a deviation in the report. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SAP §9.6 p26 lists 'participant' among parameters fitted as fixed effects together with treatment group and baseline score, and also includes baseline both as an assessment time and as a covariate. Read literally, participant fixed effects absorb the time-invariant treatment and baseline terms; the intended repeated-measures model (unstructured covariance) is nevertheless recognizable, so I rate it minor.
rows.evidence: joi240145supp1 SAP p26 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Within the same SAP paragraph: 'Parameters allowing for participant, treatment group, baseline score, time and the randomisation minimisation variables will be included (all as fixed effects except centre)' and 'All assessment times (baseline and the post-treatment time points) will be included', with baseline score also a covariate. With participant indicators as fixed effects, the treatment main effect and baseline covariate lie in the span of the participant columns and are not separately identified; including baseline as both outcome occasion and covariate is a second internal tension. The day-specific contrasts remain obtainable in some parameterizations, and the surrounding text (repeated measures, unstructured covariance, sandwich SEs) indicates a standard MMRM was intended, so the conflict is real but mainly one of wording. K minor_presentation. I considered indeterminate because the baseline-as-occasion question changes the estimand; I kept minor because the report (p4) clarifies baseline adjustment.

rows.R: RSA C v3.0 p112 and v6.0 p184 (supp1) list HHD/grip muscle strength as a secondary efficacy endpoint; R-SAP v1.0 p76 and v3.0 p109-112 make CAFS, SVC, survival the key secondaries and HHD exploratory; article p3 and eMethods p5-6 report HHD as exploratory. Outcome-status change; the R-SAP governance table (supp2 p104) gives the SAP authority on analysis matters, but the later RSA v6.0 still lists HHD as secondary. Not disclosed.
rows.evidence: joi240158supp1 pp112,184; joi240158supp2 pp76-78,104,109-112; jama_berry pp1,3; joi240158supp3 pp5-6 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Protocol regimen appendix (both v3.0, 2020, and v6.0, Nov 2022) names change in muscle strength by HHD and grip strength as a secondary efficacy endpoint alongside SVC and survival. The regimen SAPs (Mar and Jul 2022) and the report list HHD among exploratory measures and add CAFS as the first key secondary. The status change between the protocol and the report is real. It is also a plan-internal discrepancy (RSA v6.0 postdates R-SAP v3.0 yet keeps HHD secondary), which I note but which does not change the P_R classification. L substantive_difference (outcome hierarchy).

rows.R: Article p3: 'plasma NfL was prespecified to occur in samples from this regimen only'; eMethods p6 ('Plasma NfL was added later as a post-hoc analysis') and p11 (PD SAP originally specified UCH-L1, so plasma NfL 'is considered post-hoc'). R-SAP v3.0 p110/p112 lists serum and CSF NfL, not plasma NfL. Article p8 presents plasma NfL -9.5%, P=.04 as a result. Disclosed as post hoc in the supplement only; the article text contradicts it.
rows.evidence: jama_berry pp3,8; joi240158supp3 pp6,11,17; joi240158supp2 pp110,112 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The article attributes prespecification to plasma NfL; the supplied regimen SAP contains no plasma NfL analysis, and the results supplement twice calls it post hoc for this manuscript. The difference between the supplied plan and the article's claim is clear, and the report also contradicts itself (S_C), which strengthens rather than resolves the candidate. An external pharmacodynamic SAP (not supplied) is said to have named UCH-L1, not NfL. L substantive_difference: a post hoc biomarker contrast is presented as prespecified in the main text, and it is one of only two nominally significant findings.

rows.R: R-SAP v3.0 pp116-126 plans ECM sensitivity and EPP supportive DRR analyses, joint-rank SVC, multiple-imputation and death-alone CAFS/SVC rank analyses, placebo-reference MI (50 imputations), death-alone survival, and early-disease/urate/bulbar-onset/site subgroups. rows.evidence: joi240158supp2 pp113,116-117,119,121,125-126; jama_berry pp3-4,7-8; joi240158supp3 pp1,9-20,25 (text search for per-protocol, ECM, imputation, urate, site of onset, logrank, death alone). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Each named family was searched by keyword and by reading eTables 1-5 and the eFigure. Reported: FAS and regimen-only DRR, baseline-NfL-adjusted CAFS and SVC, PAV/death to week 24 by Cox, ALSFRS-R slope subgroups in eTable 4. Not reported: ECM and EPP DRR, SVC joint-rank, MI-extended and death-alone rank analyses, placebo-reference MI, death-alone and post-placebo-period survival, and the early-disease, urate, bulbar-onset and site subgroups (listed as analyzed in eMethods p13 but absent from eTable 4). rows.R: R-SAP v3.0 (22 Jul 2022) p118-119: primary CAFS inference from a rank regression adjusted for onset time, delta-FRS, riluzole, edaravone (revision history p97 states the change to an adjusted analysis). Article p3-4: Wilcoxon rank-sum, mean ranks 143.9 vs 140.5, P=.51. The report matches the superseded R-SAP v1.0 p84 (npar1way Wilcoxon). Sequence is documented, so I did not use version_timing.
rows.evidence: joi240158supp2 pp84-85 (v1.0), 97, 118-119 (v3.0); jama_berry pp3-4; joi240158supp3 p9 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The latest supplied regimen SAP specifies covariate-adjusted CAFS as the primary analysis of the first key secondary endpoint and explicitly records that revision. The report describes and reports an unadjusted Wilcoxon test. Only the baseline-NfL-adjusted CAFS sensitivity (P=.88) is given, which is a different covariate set. The difference is real against the operative SAP; it coincides with the earlier SAP version, which I record as context. L substantive_difference (analysis method of a key secondary endpoint).

rows.R: R-SAP v3.0 p117 and p121 (and v1.0 p85-86): primary survival inference by Kaplan-Meier and logrank on pooled active vs placebo in FAS, with an unadjusted Cox HR if logrank is significant. Report (p3-4, Table 2 p7, eMethods p10-12): adjusted Cox HRs and P values only; KM curves shown but no logrank result.
rows.evidence: joi240158supp2 pp85-86,117-118,121; jama_berry pp3-4,7; joi240158supp3 pp10,12 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The planned primary test for the third key secondary endpoint (logrank) is not reported in either the article or the supplement; the reported inference is an adjusted Cox model (adjusted Cox models are also mentioned in R-SAP 6.5.4, so the Cox output is not itself unplanned). The planned primary test result is absent. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Article p3 and eMethods p10: Cox covariates = prebaseline slope, months since onset, riluzole, edaravone, age (5). Table 2 footnote b p7: age, sex, time since onset, prebaseline slope, riluzole, edaravone (6, adds sex). eMethods p12 (time-to-event) again omits sex. The report contradicts itself on the model behind the printed HRs; HR values themselves are unambiguous.
rows.evidence: jama_berry pp3,7; joi240158supp3 pp10,12; joi240158supp2 p121 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Two report locations describe the covariate set for the same PAV-free survival Cox models differently (with vs without sex). It cannot be determined which was fitted. With 14 events in the pooled comparison, the covariate set can matter for the adjusted HR, so an extractor recording the adjustment set could be misled, but the printed HRs/CIs are clear. Confirmed reporting inconsistency; rated minor_presentation because it concerns the description of one covariate, not a printed value; J possible.

rows.R: Article p4 (citing eTable 2): mortality event rate 0.007/month shared placebo and 0.006/month CNM-Au8. eTable 2 p15: 0.010 (95% CrI 0.0054-0.0154) and 0.009 (0.0052-0.0150) for the same model. Differences of 30-33% are not rounding. Also noted: the article's ALSFRS-R slope CrIs (-1.176 to -0.892; -1.153 to -0.858) differ from eTable 2 (-1.181 to -0.894; -1.143 to -0.847).
rows.evidence: jama_berry p4; joi240158supp3 p15 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Same Bayesian shared-parameter model, same groups, same quantity, and the article explicitly points to eTable 2. 0.007 vs 0.010 and 0.006 vs 0.009 cannot both be correct roundings. eTable 2 median and mean are identical (0.010), so a median-versus-mean explanation fails. The slope credible intervals also differ in the third decimal between the two locations, which suggests the article text may come from a different model run. Confirmed; substantive because these are extractable posterior estimates of the primary model components; J direct.

rows.R: E changed to statistical_results: the problem is the unit of a numeric estimate. Article p4 gives -9.32 vs -8.53 'PPN per month' and difference -0.78 PPN/month; eTable 3A p16 gives the same numbers as 24-week change estimates. -9.32/5.52 months = -1.69/month, close to the slope-model values -1.73 vs -1.55/month that the article gives for the NfL-adjusted sensitivity analysis. Mislabeling overstates the monthly rate about 5.5-fold.
rows.evidence: jama_berry pp3-4; joi240158supp3 pp10,16-17 (text). Recalculation in r/p27643.R. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The article labels 24-week change estimates from the repeated-measures model (eTable 3A: '24-week Change Estimate', -9.32 [1.36], -8.53 [1.15], difference -0.78 [-4.25 to 2.68]) as monthly rates. 168 days = 5.52 months; -9.32/5.52 = -1.69 PPN/month, consistent with slope-scale values reported in the next sentence. The SVC result is the second key secondary endpoint. I treat this as a numerical/unit reporting error (statistical_results) rather than a report-internal inconsistency, per the Codebook note that numerical reporting errors belong to statistical_results. Confirmed, substantive, direct.

rows.R: Article p4: 'Of those, 4 of the 41 participants in the regimen placebo group and 2 in the shared placebo group were excluded due to having no follow-up time (1 had PAV at baseline and 1 terminated early...)'. Table 2 p7 uses 4/41 for regimen placebo and 9/162 for shared placebo, and footnote a says only 2 shared placebo participants were excluded. The parenthetical explains 2 exclusions, so '4 of the 41' must mean events. Sentence is wrong as written; Table 2 makes the intended meaning recoverable.
rows.evidence: jama_berry pp4,7 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: As written the sentence says 6 participants were excluded, which conflicts with the Table 2 denominators (41 and 162 = 164 - 2) and with its own two listed reasons. The most plausible reading is that 4 of 41 regimen placebo participants had events. Confirmed reporting error, minor because the table gives the correct denominators and event counts; J unlikely.

rows.R: R-SAP v1.0 p88-89 and v3.0 p125-126: weight <43, 43-<56, 56-<77, 77-<150, >=150 kg; delta-FRS three fixed groups (<0.47, 0.47-<1.11, >=1.11). eTable 4 p18-20 and eMethods p13: weight <56 / 56-<77 / 77-<150; dFRS median split. But M-SAP v3.0 p25 (to which the R-SAP subgroups are 'in addition') lists a dFRS median split, and M-SAP v2.0, which governs regimen C, is not supplied. Weight merge may reflect an empty <43 kg group. L indeterminate.
rows.evidence: joi240158supp2 pp25,88-89,125-126; joi240158supp3 pp13,18-20; jama_berry p8 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The weight partition differs (two planned categories merged) and the R-SAP's three-category dFRS partition is not shown, but a median split is itself in the supplied master SAP, so the reported dFRS partition is planned and the difference is rather an unreported additional partition. Whether the weight merge changed membership depends on whether anyone weighed <43 kg (not reported). Additional observation: eTable 4 labels the El Escorial subgroup 'Definite and <18 months' vs 'Not Definite and <18 months', whereas both plans define the comparison as 'definite and <18 months vs not both'; the label suggests a different complement. Retained as a difference; L indeterminate because the extent cannot be established.

rows.R: Protocol RSA C v3.0 p112 and v6.0 p184: exploratory 'difference in the proportion of patients experiencing a >=6-point decline in ALSFRS-R ... from Baseline to Week 24'. R-SAP v1.0 p78 and v3.0 p111: time to first >=6-point decline, a composite with death or death equivalent, censored at last ALSFRS-R assessment. A week-24 binary proportion and a time-to-first-event composite including death are different endpoints. The report (p3) follows the SAP (time to decline).
rows.evidence: joi240158supp1 pp112,184; joi240158supp2 pp78,104,111,113 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The two plan documents define the six-point decline endpoint with different variable type, estimand and event set (death included only in the SAP). The SAP governance table (p104) makes the R-SAP authoritative on analysis, which explains which definition was used, but the plan documents remain inconsistent, and the later protocol version (v6.0, Nov 2022) retains the proportion definition. Exploratory endpoint, but the conflict changes what is measured; K substantive_inconsistency.

rows.R: eTable 3B p17: plasma pooled -9.5 (-18.0, 0) P=0.04 and 60 mg -10.5 (-20, 0) P=0.04 are consistent with rounding (CI-implied P 0.039/0.040; article gives -17.8 to -0.4, Figure 3 -17.8 to -0.5). Serum 60 mg -27.4 (-45.1, -0.7) P=0.05 is not: the estimate lies 4.5 units off the CI midpoint (-22.9), unlike the other rows (offset <0.1), and the CI excludes 0 while P=.05. Probable typo in that row.
rows.evidence: joi240158supp3 p17; jama_berry p8 (text and Figure 3 caption). Recalculation r/p27643.R.
rows.rationale: Recomputed SE from each CI: plasma pooled z=-2.07, P=0.039; plasma 60 mg z=-2.06, P=0.040; so the printed '0' upper bounds are rounded small negatives and P=.04 is compatible. The article itself gives three versions of the plasma upper bound (-0.4 text, -0.5 figure, 0 table), a minor display inconsistency. For serum, pooled and 30 mg rows are symmetric (midpoints -26.45 and -25.45 vs estimates -26.4, -25.5), but the 60 mg row is not (midpoint -22.9 vs -27.4); with the printed CI the implied P is about 0.016, not 0.05. So one row is probably mistyped (estimate or a bound). Exploratory dose-specific biomarker contrast: probable issue, minor; J possible.

rows.R: Article p8/Figure 3: serum NfL placebo +30.8%, CNM-Au8 +0.4%, difference -23.2% (95% CI -39.5 to -2.5), P=.03. eTable 3B p17: placebo 26.8, difference -26.4 (-50.3, -2.6), P=0.03, labeled % change/GMR. The eTable values are log-scale x100: exp(0.268)-1=30.7%, exp(-0.264)-1=-23.2%, exp(-0.503)-1=-39.5%, exp(-0.026)-1=-2.6%. Plasma rows are on the back-transformed scale. Serum rows are on the wrong scale for their label.
rows.evidence: jama_berry p8; joi240158supp3 p17 (text). Recalculation r/p27643.R. Card read after judgment (the card raises the log-scale explanation; my check reproduces it).
rows.rationale: Article geometric means: 56.5/43.1-1 = +31.1% (printed 30.8, model-based), (60.8/60.6)/(56.5/43.1)-1 = -23.5% (printed -23.2). Plasma eTable row reproduces as a ratio: (0.977/1.079)-1 = -9.45%. Serum eTable rows instead equal 100 x log-scale values; back-transforming them reproduces the article exactly. The footnote states the NfL values were exponentiated back, so the serum rows are mislabeled/untransformed. Two different numbers for the same nominally significant exploratory contrast (-23.2% vs -26.4%; placebo +30.8% vs +26.8%). Confirmed; substantive for extraction; J direct. I first suspected a difference-of-percentages scale; the log-scale explanation fits all serum rows, including CIs, better.

rows.R: M-SAP v3.0 §6.2 p50: prose says 'the power and estimated DRR decrease as the rate of mortality increases', but Table 6.2.1 shows mean estimated DRR rising (0.71/0.72/0.75 for mortality HR 1.0; 0.72/0.75/0.81 for HR 1.3) while power falls. The next sentences give the correct values and say the functional treatment effect decreases, so the intended meaning is clear. Wording slip in design operating characteristics.
rows.evidence: joi240158supp2 p50 (text; table read from text layer). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Real internal inconsistency in the plan's description of design operating characteristics (estimated DRR increases, i.e., less estimated benefit, as mortality rises). Operating characteristics bear on the design, so I retain rather than exclude, but the table and the following sentence make the meaning clear: K minor_presentation. Caveat: M-SAP v3.0 (Feb 2023) states it applies to regimens initiated under protocol v5.0; regimen C was governed by M-SAP v2.0, not supplied.

rows.R: M-SAP p59: 'CAFS p-value of -' at line end, '.3675)' on the next line, in an illustrative example trial (Example Trial 4); the adjacent figure prints 0.3675. A line-end dash in an illustration, not a design element of this trial; no conflict that matters for the plan.
rows.evidence: joi240158supp2 pp58-59 (text; p59 rendered at 200 dpi to inspect the dash).
rows.rationale: The rendered page shows a dash at the right margin before a line break, followed by '.3675'. Whether a stray hyphen or a typed minus, it occurs in narrative about an illustrative example trial in the operating-characteristics section, and the null-result reading is clear from the same sentence and the figure. It does not affect any design or analysis element the reported analysis depends on, so I exclude it (guide 6.3: non-design content).

rows.R: R-SAP v3.0 §5.6 p112: serum/CSF NfL values below the limit of quantitation imputed at the LOQ. eMethods p11: serum values <LOQ imputed using the assay LOD. Different substitution value for the same condition. Relevant because the serum NfL result was sensitive to a very low baseline value (article p8; eMethods p12).
rows.evidence: joi240158supp2 p112; joi240158supp3 pp11-12; jama_berry p8 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Plan and report specify different replacement values for below-LOQ serum NfL. Neither the numeric LOQ/LOD nor the number of affected samples is given, so the numerical impact cannot be computed. Because the serum NfL contrast changed from -23.2% (P=.03) to -9.7% (P=.05) after excluding one very low baseline value, low-value handling is consequential for this analysis. L substantive_difference (data-handling rule for an analyzed variable).

rows.R: Protocol v5.0 p43 (10.1.1): painTRAINER sessions take 45-60 min; p44 (10.1.2): coach sessions take 60 min. Main p3 and TIDieR supp3 pp3-4: painTRAINER 30-45 min, coach 45-60 min. Session number (8) and 12-week window unchanged. Described per-session dose is shorter in the report for both arms (non-overlapping for painTRAINER); may reflect a revised completion-time estimate rather than changed content. Card agrees.
rows.evidence: Main p3 (text); protocol supp1 pp43-44 (text layer encoded; OCR at 300 dpi and 110-dpi renders read visually); TIDieR supp3 pp3-4 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The protocol describes each online painTRAINER session as taking 45-60 minutes and each coach session as 60 minutes. The article and the TIDieR supplement describe painTRAINER sessions as 30-45 minutes and coach sessions as 45-60 minutes. The number of sessions, weekly cadence and 12-week completion window are the same. For painTRAINER the two ranges do not overlap; for the coach arm the reported range extends below the planned fixed length. This is a difference in the described intervention procedure (contact time per session), which affects extraction of intervention dose (8 x 45-60 = 6-8 h planned vs 8 x 30-45 = 4-6 h reported for painTRAINER). Neither document says whether the figures are design estimates or observed times, and the self-paced program content may be unchanged, so the difference is descriptive only. Coded substantive_difference because the per-session dose description differs for both arms; another reviewer could reasonably treat it as minor_presentation.

rows.R: Main p4: painTRAINER '371 (43%) completed at least 6 sessions'. Figure 1 p5: 776 randomized; 371 + 156 + 249 = 776. 371/776 = 47.8% (printed 43%); 371/527 initiators = 70.4%. Other three adherence percentages reproduce (527/776 = 67.9%, 660/778 = 84.8%, 548/778 = 70.4%). Count is correct, percentage wrong. Card agrees.
rows.evidence: Main pp4-5 (text; Figure 1 flow counts from text layer). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Text: 'Of those randomized to the painTRAINER group, 527 (68%) completed at least 1 session and 371 (43%) completed at least 6 sessions (therapeutic dose).' Figure 1 gives 776 randomized to painTRAINER with 371 completing 6-8 sessions, 156 completing 1-5 and 249 none (sum 776). Recomputed: 371/776 = 0.478 (47.8%); 527/776 = 67.9% (printed 68%, correct). The parallel health coach figures reproduce (660/778 = 84.8% printed 85%; 548/778 = 70.4% printed 70%). No denominator gives 43%: 371/527 = 70.4%; 371/863 would be needed. The count and denominator are printed, so the correct value is recoverable, and the qualitative point (lower adherence with painTRAINER) is unchanged, although the gap to health coach is overstated (43% vs 70% printed; 48% vs 70% correct). Confirmed, minor_presentation; downstream possible because adherence percentages are commonly extracted.

rows.R: Main p4 and Table 3 note d (p11): SMD = adjusted MD / SD of UC change at that time point, so the three contrasts at a time point share one denominator. Recomputed for all 21 rows: implied SD (MD/SMD) differs across the three columns of one row (e.g., social 3 mo: 6.7, 150, 3.5), 4 SMDs have the opposite sign to their MD, HC-PT SMD is -0.08 to -0.13 where MD is 0.0, and SMD(HC-PT) is not SMD(HC-UC) - SMD(PT-UC) in 17 rows. SMD columns cannot follow the stated definition. Also: text p7 quotes 3-month SMDs -0.26/-0.36, which are the 6-month values in Table 3 (3-month: -0.25/-0.34). Card agrees.
rows.evidence: Main pp4, 7, 10-11 (text layer; Table 3 checked against the rendered page). R script smd.R in working folder. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Footnote d and the methods define the SMD as the adjusted between-group mean difference divided by the SD of change in the usual care plus group at the given time point. Under this definition all three contrasts at one outcome/time share one positive denominator, so (i) MD/SMD must be constant across the three columns, (ii) the SMD must have the sign of its MD, and (iii) SMD(HC-PT) = SMD(HC-UC) - SMD(PT-UC). Recomputation over all 21 outcome/time rows (63 tuples): implied SD varies within row far beyond rounding (pain severity 3 mo 1.60, 1.18, and 0 for HC-PT where MD = -0.0 but SMD = -0.13; social role 3 mo 6.7, 150, 3.5; PGIC pain 3 mo 1.13, 1.45, 0.54); sign conflicts in 4 tuples (physical 3 mo HC-UC MD +0.7 vs SMD -0.02; physical 6 mo HC-PT -0.3 vs +0.22; physical 12 mo HC-PT -0.1 vs +0.27; PGIC pain 12 mo HC-PT +0.1 vs -0.29); additivity fails in most rows (social 3 mo 0.12/0.01/0.20; physical 6 mo 0.15/0.02/0.22). For the social and physical rows the SMD pattern looks as if the HC-UC and HC-PT columns were exchanged or shifted, but no single permutation reconciles all rows, so the intended values cannot be recovered. The 14 out-of-interval points (C010) and 18 reversed intervals are further manifestations. In addition, the Results text (p7) quotes 3-month SMDs of -0.26 (painTRAINER) and -0.36 (health coach), which are the 6-month values in Table 3; the 3-month values printed are -0.25 and -0.34. SMDs are the standardized effects most likely to be extracted for meta-analysis, and the text uses them to characterize effects as small or modest. Confirmed, substantive, direct.

Interpreting the en dash as a minus sign lost in typesetting gives RD intervals [-1/U, 1/L]; the implied lower limits (-0.54, -1.32, -1.75, -2.63, -1.49 and -1.27 percentage points) agree closely with the lower RD limits implied by applying the RR limits to the painTRAINER percentage (-0.66, -1.44, -1.70, -2.57, -1.48, -1.19). So the eTable 3 intervals are not 95% Wald intervals for the printed P values (likely +/-1 SE intervals, or P from a 1.96-fold SE). rows.rationale: For eTable 3 (linear imputation model), I computed SE from each CI as width/3.92, the CI-implied z and P, and the z implied by the printed P. For every row with an exact P the ratio z_CI/z_P lies between 1.77 and 2.45 (median 1.94), with deviations explained by two-decimal rounding of small estimates; e.g., Time 6M 0.13 (0.07-0.19) gives CI-implied P = 2e-5 vs printed .025; Pattern 2 -0.28 (-0.47 to -0.08) gives .005 vs .150. Treating each printed interval as estimate +/- 1 SE reproduces the printed P values closely (Pattern 2 0.151 vs .150; Pattern 1 0.225 vs .226; Site 3 0.070 vs .069; second AA 0.075 vs .077; Male 0.0034 vs .003). A constant factor of about 1.96 is not what a different robust or joint variance estimator would produce (that would vary by coefficient), so the intervals or the P values in eTable 3 were computed with a misplaced critical value. Seven flagged eTable 3 rows are instances of this. The other three flagged rows reproduce: eTable 4 age 1.15 (1.00-1.33), CI-implied P .055 vs printed .046 and second AA 1.16 (1.00-1.33) .041 vs .046, eTable 5 PEG 0.96 (0.92-1.00) .055 vs .037; all are compatible once the limits printed as 1/1.00 are allowed their rounding range. So the arm labels of the raw columns are permuted, and the two 'HC' PGIC cells that look like medians actually sit in the painTRAINER column. Anyone extracting arm-level follow-up summaries from eTable 11 would take the wrong statistic and the wrong arm. Confirmed, substantive, direct. rows.R: Main p3: PROMIS-29 has 7 domains (raw 4-20 each), higher scores better in some and worse in others. Main p6 and eTable 4 (supp3 p15) report one PROMIS-29 score (levodopa 66 (14) text, 64.74 (14.33) eTable 4; placebo 65 (14) / 65.11 (13.79)) and MD -0.37 (-3.34 to 2.61). No scoring rule, range or direction for this single score in the article, protocol (p70 v1.4 / OCR) or SAP. A sum of mixed-direction raw domains is not interpretable, and the sign of the MD cannot be read. Text 66 also does not round from 64.74. Card agrees; the text-table mismatch is additional.
rows.evidence: Main pp3, 6 (text); supp3 p15 eTable 4 (text); protocol supp1 p70 (OCR, 300 dpi); SAP supp2 p5 (OCR; no text layer). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The methods define PROMIS-29 as seven 4-item domains with raw scores of 4-20 and mixed direction (higher is better for physical function and social roles, worse for anxiety, depression, fatigue, sleep disturbance and pain interference), and pain intensity is a separate 0-10 item (protocol p70). The results nevertheless report a single PROMIS-29 mean per arm (about 65 in both groups, which is in the range of a raw sum of seven domains, 28-140) and an adjusted mean difference of -0.37. Neither the article, the protocol nor the SAP defines a PROMIS-29 total, its range, or whether any domains were reverse-scored, and PROMIS-29 has no standard total score (summary scores such as PROPr or physical/mental health summaries require a specified algorithm). The scale and direction of the reported outcome therefore cannot be identified, so the effect cannot be interpreted beyond 'no detectable difference' and cannot be extracted for pooling. In addition, the text gives the levodopa mean as 66 (14) whereas eTable 4 gives 64.74 (14.33), which rounds to 65; the placebo values agree. Confirmed reporting issue (undefined outcome scoring); substantive because the outcome measure itself is undefined for any downstream use; downstream possible (secondary, exploratory outcome).

Death-inclusive analyses (estimand 3, -0.98; win ratio 1.06; post hoc estimand 10 with FMA = 0 for deaths, -0.03) are reported as supportive and agree with the primary. rows.rationale: Both protocol versions specify a mixed-effects model with a random intercept for center; v1.4 adds stroke type (ischemic vs hemorrhagic) as a fixed effect. The SAP (finalized after the last visit) specifies a linear model with baseline FMA and treatment only, and the published code fits exactly lm(fma_affected.Visit_3 ~ fma_affected.Visit_1.cent + medication) on each imputed data set. Randomization used center-stratified minimization, so omitting center from the analysis model departs both from the protocol and from the usual practice of adjusting for stratification factors; stroke type was also prespecified in the final protocol. With center imbalance minimized the point estimate may change little, but the standard error and the estimand of the planned model are not reported. The article's general statement about protocol-SAP differences in terminology does not cover this model change. Substantive difference in the primary model (descriptive).

rows.R: SAP p11 section 6: missing secondary outcomes imputed as for the primary (100 MICE imputations); only harm outcomes not imputed. Main p5: mRS and PRAI missing data not imputed; supp3 p7 lists these as SAP deviations (deaths set to mRS 6; PRAI not imputed). eTable 4: mRS n = 596, PRAI n = 546 vs 582 for other secondaries. Disclosed (supp3 p7). Card agrees.
rows.evidence: SAP supp2 p11 (OCR and render); main p5 (text); supp3 pp7, 15 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The SAP applies multiple imputation to all secondary outcomes other than harm outcomes. The report did not impute the mRS or the patient-reported assessment of relevance of motor improvement: deceased participants were assigned mRS 6 (the scale's definition of death, which is reasonable) and missing PRAI responses were left missing, giving analysis sets of 596 and 546 rather than the 582 used for the other secondary outcomes. Whether surviving participants with missing mRS were imputed or dropped is not stated; the main text's blanket statement is broader than the supplement's death-only explanation. The supplement discloses both as deviations from the SAP. Retained as a disclosed difference in missing-data handling for two secondary outcomes. Also noted: the PRAI placebo numerator is 52/270 in the text (p6) but 51/270 (18.89%) in eTable 4.

rows.R: SAP p12 7.2 and addendum pp14-15 (4 Oct 2024): 7 prespecified subgroup interactions (age, sex, distal motor function, cortical dysfunction, SSRI, stroke type, baseline FMA <median vs >=median) in a forest plot; SAP p11: center and treatment-by-center terms in the main model; protocol v1.4 p86 11.4.3: stroke-type interaction and covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses. rows.evidence: SAP supp2 pp11-12, 14-15 (OCR; p11 render); protocol supp1 p86 (render); main pp4-5, 7 (text); supp3 pp1, 18, 25, 27 (text; eFigures 5, 7 and eTables 7-8 rendered at 100 dpi). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The SAP prespecifies seven subgroup analyses of the primary estimand, each with a subgroup-by-treatment interaction and presented as a forest plot, with directional hypotheses recorded in the ICEMAN addendum dated 4 October 2024 (before database closure). It also specifies a model including center and a treatment-by-center interaction, and the final protocol adds a treatment-by-stroke-type interaction and covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses (age, sex, dementia, hand/wrist movement, cortical dysfunction, fatigue, SSRI, extrapyramidal symptoms, impetus). The supplied report contains none of these results: the supplement index lists estimand tables, a continuous baseline-FMA interaction and spline model (eTables 7-8, post hoc), a center boxplot (eFigure 5, called post hoc in the article although the protocol and SAP prespecified a graphical display by center) and a post hoc forest plot with two estimands and one baseline-FMA subgroup (<=35 vs >35). The last is close to the prespecified baseline-severity subgroup (overall median 34) but uses a fixed cut point and is labelled post hoc. The article states that prespecified analyses were performed as outlined in the SAP. Planned subgroup and center analyses of the primary outcome are not reported; retained as a substantive difference. The complete-case (estimand 2) and per-protocol-type analyses (estimands 6, 7; PH2) are reported, so the omission concerns the subgroup, interaction and covariate analyses.

rows.R: Main p6 Table 2 (rendered): levodopa top-level SAE categories sum to 143 vs parent 126; placebo 139 vs 129. Infection subtypes sum to 59 vs 55 (levodopa) and 52 vs 44 (placebo). Stroke (15+1, 18+1) and cardiac (5+5+2, 1+2+0) subtypes reconcile; AEs of interest reconcile (79, 67). No note says an event may count in several categories, and 'Other (none of the above)' implies exclusive coding. Counts are integers, so rounding does not apply; all four comparisons fail, not only the two the card registered.
rows.evidence: Main pp6-7 (text; Table 2 rendered at 200 dpi to check indentation); supp3 pp16-17 eTables 5-6 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Recomputed: levodopa 55+16+5+12+4+4+6+3+3+2+1+0+32 = 143 vs 126 events; placebo 44+19+10+3+7+5+2+6+4+2+3+0+34 = 139 vs 129. Infection subtypes: levodopa 27+15+5+0+1+11 = 59 vs 55; placebo 17+15+7+2+2+9 = 52 vs 44. Subtypes of stroke and cardiac events add exactly to their parents, and the prespecified AEs of interest add exactly to 79 and 67, so the table is otherwise additive. The rendered table indents only the stroke subtypes; cardiac subtypes, 'Fall', 'Fracture' and 'Traumatic intracerebral hemorrhage' are printed at the category level, which makes the hierarchy itself ambiguous (Trauma 4 = Fall 4). An event with several diagnoses or infection sites could be counted in more than one category, which would explain sums above the parent totals, but the table does not say so, and the card's precision allowance of +/-0.5 per summand is not appropriate for integer counts. The arm totals (126, 129; eTable 5 n = 255) and infection totals (55, 44) are consistent with the text, so the overall SAE picture is clear; the category breakdown cannot be reconciled as printed. Probable issue (multiple coding unstated), minor, downstream possible for category-level harms extraction. eTable 6 also gives n = 145 overall for prespecified AEs vs 67 + 79 = 146 (outside this candidate).

rows.R: Protocol v2.0 Table 4 p22 (OCR and rotated render; text layer garbled): age <75 row (25%, active 2.96%, control 1.18%) prints 34% power at N=5000, 2p<0.01. Inverting the continuity-corrected (Fleiss) sample-size formula gives 28.6%; the same method reproduces the row's other cells (41.8/20.5/52.1 vs 41/20/52) and the 12 sample sizes. The 5000/0.01 column runs 0.5-2 points high in other rows too (e.g., female 72.9 vs 75), so a small method difference may contribute, but the <75 gap (5.4 points) is the largest. Design meaning unchanged (subgroup underpowered either way).

rows.rationale: Computed per-arm n = fraction x N / 2 and solved the Fleiss continuity-corrected formula for power. Results: <80: 89.0/72.8/94.9/84.5 vs printed 89/73/95/85; >=80: 95.9/86.8/98.6/94.3 vs 96/87/99/95; <75: 41.8/20.5/52.1/28.6 vs 41/20/52/34; >=75: 99.6/97.7/99.9/99.5 vs 100/98/100/100; males 97.9/92.3/99.4/97.3 vs 98/92/99/98; females 80.5/59.6/89.0/72.9 vs 80/60/89/75. Total sample sizes also reproduce within about 1%. An uncorrected normal calculation gives about 36% for the cell but fails the row's 4000/0.01 cell. The <75 cell is therefore probably a slip within the plan's own table, though the systematic small upward drift in that column means the method used for that column is not fully known. Retained as a plan-internal inconsistency; minor because the subgroup is clearly underpowered at either value and the planned analysis is unaffected.

rows.R: Moderate hyperglycemia: article p3 and Manual ch.7 p39 = 120-180 mg/dL on 2 consecutive determinations >=6 h apart OR >2 determinations within 24 h with no intervening normal value. SAP §3.2.4.1 p11 = 120-180 on two determinations >=6 h apart (no second pathway); Manual Appendix A toxicity table p59 = 2 consecutive determinations >=6 h apart (no second pathway). Article p3 also defines severe as simply >180 mg/dL, whereas SAP/manual require 2 determinations or insulin. Definition behind the main safety finding (66.7% vs 49.8%, RR 1.33) differs from the SAP.
rows.evidence: jama_ambalavanan pp1,3,6; joi250072supp4 eTable 3 p5 (OCR); joi250072supp2 manual pp39,59 (OCR); joi250072supp3 SAP p11 (OCR). Supplement text layers are font-encoded, so all supplement pages were OCR'd at 300 dpi. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The report's moderate-hyperglycemia definition adds a qualification route (more than two readings within 24 h) that the SAP and the manual's own toxicity table do not contain; the report matches only the manual's chapter 7 narrative, so the plan documents are themselves inconsistent. Three readings 1 h apart would qualify under the report but not the SAP. The report's severe threshold also omits the repeat-determination requirement. Because hyperglycemia is the only safety outcome that differed and is in the abstract, the difference in qualifying definition is material to what the reported proportion means; the numerical consequence cannot be computed. L substantive_difference.

rows.evidence: jama_ambalavanan pp3,6,8; joi250072supp1 protocol pp21,25 (OCR); joi250072supp3 SAP pp32-35,39 (OCR). Card read after judgment.

These are different estimands (cumulative vs category-specific odds). The report gives no reason or PO test result. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SAP §9.4.1 p38: primary analysis replicated in mITT, PP and SAF (as-treated); §9.4.2: model adding baseline BPD predictors (birth weight, sex, race/ethnicity) and imbalanced covariates; §7.7 p29: interactions of treatment with site/center, randomization GA stratum, race, sex in the primary robust Poisson model; protocol §5.1 p25: prespecified analyses by treatment received. All 8 marked rows reproduce log-Wald intervals, not exact (Fisher conditional) ones: e.g., PDA surgery 5/319 vs 3/308: printed 1.62 (0.38-6.83); Wald 0.384-6.833; exact 0.312-10.51. SAE ETT 1 vs 1: printed 0.06-15.66; Wald 0.061-15.61; exact 0.012-76.5. Method label wrong; intervals narrower than exact. All include 1, so no inference changes.

rows.R: Protocol synopsis p6 and §3.2 p15: primary endpoint = any of >=5% weight loss, >=4% weight loss + >=150 min/wk PA, or >=0.2% HbA1c reduction. Disclosed in the 'Summary of Changes to SAP' (supp1 p86: incident diabetes 'was not prespecified' as failure) and eTable 13 (15 participants with diabetes-range HbA1c). The article presents it as the primary outcome without labeling the added condition as post hoc.
rows.evidence: joi250084supp1 pp6,15,86 (protocol text layer font-encoded; OCR at 300 dpi); jama_mathioudakis pp1,3-4; joi250084supp2 pp29-30,56 (text). Card read after judgment.

The change alters the primary composite definition after the plan and is disclosed only in the supplement's SAP-change table; how many of the 15 listed participants would otherwise have succeeded is not reported. Disclosed; retained per the fixed review decision. L substantive_difference (primary outcome definition).

rows.R: Protocol p6 and §3.2 p15 (post-amendment 1.4 text): PA branch = average >=150 min/wk over months 6-11 from monthly actigraphy. Supp2 p13: weekly MVPA summed over all valid periods and divided by available periods 'maximum of 11 post-baseline visits', i.e., averaged 'throughout the 12-month follow-up period'. Article p3/Figure 3 do not state a 6-11 window. Not listed in the SAP-change table (p86-87).
rows.evidence: joi250084supp1 pp6,15,80-81 (OCR); joi250084supp2 pp13,49 (text); jama_mathioudakis pp3,7-8. Card read after judgment.

The report never states that a separate 6-11 calculation was used for the binary branch, so the planned window cannot be confirmed; I record the difference as described. The supplied amendment log dates the change and its rationale, and the report follows it (35/130 = 26.9% in each arm). Under guide section 6.4, a later plan version containing the reported feature removes the plan-report difference; version_timing does not apply because the sequence is resolved. Excluded.

rows.R: Supp2 p13: average weekly MVPA = MVPA summed over valid wear periods divided by 'the number of available wear periods (maximum of 11)'; same page and eTable 8b p49 / eTable 18a p30: noncompliant or non-wear weeks are assigned 0 minutes. Zeros add nothing to the sum, so the zero rule matters only if those weeks enter the denominator; the text does not say they do. Either reading is possible; the description is ambiguous rather than demonstrably wrong.
rows.evidence: joi250084supp2 pp13,30,49 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: With v valid and z zero-filled periods, dividing by v ignores the stated worst-case rule; dividing by v+z implements it. Example: 200 min in one week and one non-wear week gives 200 vs 100 min/wk, on either side of 150. The worst-case rationale only makes sense with the larger denominator, which suggests that was intended, but the formula as written uses 'available' periods. Indeterminate; the PA average defines one primary-composite branch, so J possible.

An adjusted RD within each imputation could differ, but the table and methods (supp1 p88, supp2 p30) describe no outcome-model covariates. NI conclusion unchanged (-11.5 > -15).

The imputation model includes covariates, but that does not make the analysis model adjusted. Probable issue (an adjusted or otherwise different estimator is a possible but undocumented explanation). Substantive for extraction because the sensitivity estimate's sign differs from what its own arm risks imply; J possible.

The report contradicts itself on whether center is in the model behind sHR 1.02 (0.74-1.39); the estimate itself is clear.
rows.evidence: jama_combes pp2-3,6 (text); joi250087supp2 SAP p6 (scanned; OCR at 300 dpi). Card read after judgment.

Confirmed reporting inconsistency; minor because it concerns the model description rather than a printed value; J possible (adjustment set is recorded in extraction).

rows.R: SAP §2.2 p4 and §3.6 p7 (OCR): organ failure = SOFA score >2 in at least one of six organ systems. Article p3: days alive without organ failure = SOFA 0-1 for each component, i.e., failure at component score >=2; eTable 3 footnote (supp3 p6): cardiovascular failure-free = cardiovascular SOFA <2. Protocol p14-15 gives no threshold. Threshold differs by one point.
rows.evidence: joi250087supp2 pp4,7 (OCR); jama_combes p3; joi250087supp3 pp5-6; joi250087supp1 pp14-15 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Under the SAP a component score of 2 is not failure; under the report it is. This changes the count of organ-failure and organ-failure-free days (eTable 3: 12 vs 14 free days; 9 vs 12 days with failure). Not disclosed. L substantive_difference (outcome definition).

rows.R: SAP p4/p7-8 and protocol p14-15: ECMO-free days between inclusion and D30/D60 and ventilator-free days to D30 and D60. Report: Table 2 p6 gives ECMO-free days by day 30 only; eTable 3 p5 gives MV-free days by day 30 only; no D60 free-day results in the article or supplement.
rows.evidence: joi250087supp1 pp14-15 (text); joi250087supp2 pp4,7-8 (OCR); jama_combes pp1,3,6; joi250087supp3 pp1,5-6 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Searched the article and all supplement tables (contents list p1): day-60 ECMO-free and ventilator-free days are not reported, although day-60 mortality and MACE are. Planned secondary outcomes at a planned time point are absent. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SAP p8 (OCR): LV function compared by Global Net Benefit on a hierarchical composite (death, heart transplant, LVEF improvement >30%) with bootstrap CI. Report eTable 3 p5: median LVEF 45 vs 40%, difference 5 (-0 to 10), with last pre-death LVEF carried for patients who died (footnote a). No net-benefit result anywhere.
rows.evidence: joi250087supp2 p8 (OCR); joi250087supp1 pp14-15; joi250087supp3 pp5-6; jama_combes p3. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The planned estimand (net benefit over a death/transplant/LVEF hierarchy) is replaced by a marginal median LVEF difference, which also imputes the last LVEF for deaths rather than ranking death worst. Different estimand and handling of death. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol p14-15 and article p3: MACE includes dialysis. SAP p4/p7 and eFigure 4 title (supp3 p13): MACE = death, transplant, LVAD, stroke, HF rehospitalization (no dialysis). eTable 3 p5 lists 'Dialysis by day 30' as a MACE component (29 vs 38), but the 30-day MACE totals are 35 vs 36; 38 placebo dialysis events exceed the 36 MACE total, so the reported totals cannot include dialysis. The report's stated definition differs from the composite actually tabulated.
rows.evidence: joi250087supp1 pp14-15 (text); joi250087supp2 pp4,7 (OCR); jama_combes p3; joi250087supp3 pp1,5-6,13 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Plan documents disagree (protocol with dialysis, final SAP without); the reported totals follow the SAP while the article's definition and eTable 3 component list follow the protocol. Arithmetic check: placebo dialysis by day 30 = 38/104 > MACE 36/104, impossible if dialysis were a component. Composite definition change relative to the protocol, plus a report-internal inconsistency. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol p14-15 (v1.1; same in later versions): primary and secondary endpoints in predefined subgroups AMI, myocarditis, post-cardiac surgery and post-cardiac arrest. SAP has no subgroup section. Article p4 and Figure 3 p7: 'predefined subgroups (ie, minimization stratification factor)': AMI, myocarditis, postcardiotomy, Other; cardiac arrest is folded into Other (eTable 6: 5 vs 1 patients). No post-arrest subgroup result.
rows.evidence: joi250087supp1 pp14-15,17 (text); joi250087supp2 pp1-9 (OCR, whole SAP); jama_combes pp4,7; joi250087supp3 pp9,18. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The planned post-cardiac-arrest subgroup is replaced by a heterogeneous 'Other' group containing 42 patients of whom 6 had cardiac arrest, and the report labels this partition predefined. Different subgroup definition; L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SAP §3.6 pp7-8: each secondary outcome to be tested (log-rank/Wilcoxon) and analyzed with a model adjusted for cardiogenic-shock etiology (Cox for mortality, ICU/hospital stay, MACE; general linear model for free days). Report: Table 2 p6 and eTable 3 give unadjusted RRs and bootstrap median/mean differences, P values omitted 'because of multiple testing concerns' (except abstract P for ECMO duration, ICU stay, 60-day mortality); no etiology-adjusted secondary estimates.
rows.evidence: joi250087supp2 pp7-9 (OCR); joi250087supp1 protocol analysis pages 35-37 (text); jama_combes pp1,4,6-7; joi250087supp3 pp5-6,11,13 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Planned adjusted secondary analyses are not reported; the reported effect measures (unadjusted RR, bootstrap differences) differ from the planned models. In addition, the abstract and p4 give P values (.53, .42, .78) for secondaries while Table 2 footnote says P values are not reported for secondaries, a minor internal inconsistency. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Supplement 1 (text layer font-encoded; OCR): protocol v4.0 p16: 178 SMS, 4-5/day months 1-2, 2-3/day months 3-4, 1-2/week months 5-6. Protocol v6.0 (latest) p53: 134 SMS but 4-5/day months 1-2, 1-2/day months 3-4, 1/week months 5-6, a schedule that cannot total 134 (months 1-2 alone >=240). SAP p80: 3-4/day month 1, ... 1/month last four months. Article p1/p3: 134 messages, 100 in month 1, 30 in month 2, 4 monthly. Report matches the SAP, not the latest protocol schedule.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp16,53,77,80 (OCR at 300 dpi; TOC p1 identifies v4.0, v6.0, change log, SAP, SMS log); jama_zahid pp1,3. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Intervention dose and schedule are planned conduct elements. The latest protocol's schedule (and its internal total) differ from what the report says was delivered; only the SAP describes the reported schedule. The change log (p77) does not list an SMS schedule change. L substantive_difference (intervention delivery). The plan documents are also inconsistent among themselves.

rows.R: Protocol v4.0 p11 and v6.0 p49 (OCR): include current daily smokers OR those who 'have only stopped or reduced smoking (less than daily) since diagnosed with TB'; exclusions: <15 y, retreatment/MDR/miliary/extrapulmonary TB, current pharmacotherapy, unable to consent. Article p2: daily smoking (>=1 puff on >=25 of last 30 days) required; Figure 1 p4 and eTable 1 also exclude 'cannot read and no one at home can read SMS' (236) and 'not current smoker' (7069). The recent-quitter route is absent and a literacy criterion is added.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp11,49 (OCR); jama_zahid pp1-2,4; joi250093supp2 p3 (text). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The reported eligibility narrows the planned smoking criterion (patients who cut down after TB diagnosis were eligible in the plan) and adds an SMS-reading criterion not in the plan's lists. Both change the trial population for a cessation outcome. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SMS log in Supplement 1 pp101-104 (OCR): enrollment is Q(-8); message 6 on day 2 sets a quit date '7 days from today'; message 40 'Today is your QUIT DATE' on the 8th day since joining. Article p3: quit date 'set 5 days after enrollment'. The quit date anchors the continuous-abstinence definition ('since the quit date').
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp101,103,104,109 (OCR); jama_zahid p3. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Planned quit day is day 8 after enrollment (7 days after day 2), reported as 5 days after enrollment. Because the primary outcome counts tobacco use since the quit date, the difference affects the outcome window, not only the intervention calendar. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol v4.0 p8, v6.0 p47 and SAP p84 (OCR): smokeless-tobacco users verified with NicAlert urine strips, level <3 (about 100-200 ng/mL cotinine) = abstinent. Article p3: a rapid cotinine test cassette (Hangzhou AllTest) with a negative result = abstinent. Different device and decision threshold for verifying the primary outcome in concomitant smokeless users (58 at baseline). Not disclosed as a change.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp8,47,84 (OCR); jama_zahid pp3,5 (Table 1). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Planned graded semiquantitative criterion versus reported binary cassette result with unstated cutoff; equivalence cannot be established. Affects primary-outcome classification for the smokeless-tobacco subgroup. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol v4.0 §11.2.2 p28 and v6.0 §28.2.2 p66 (OCR): GLMM with log link, Poisson distribution, cluster random intercept, crude and adjusted RRs. SAP p91-92 and article p3: mixed-effects logistic regression with site random effect, results expressed as RR. The change log (p77) does not mention the model change. Report follows the SAP.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp28,66,77,91-92 (OCR); jama_zahid p3. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Model family and link for the primary analysis differ between protocol (log-Poisson, which estimates RR directly) and SAP/report (logit, which estimates OR). The SAP is dated after the protocol v6.0 (March 2025, after last follow-up in January 2025). L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Methods p3: mixed-effects logistic regression; Table 2 p6 reports 'Crude RR'. Crude risk ratios from the printed counts do not match: primary 300/720 vs 55/360 = 2.73 (Wald 2.11-3.53) vs printed crude RR 3.0 (2.0-4.9); TB success 643/720 vs 308/360 = 1.04 vs printed 1.2 (0.9-1.6); eTable 9 TB success 92.5% vs 92.5% = 1.00 vs printed crude RR 1.1. Also eTable 8 'All' unadjusted RR 2.890 (1.983-4.709) differs from Table 2 crude ITT 3.0 (2.0-4.9) but equals the PP row 2.9 (2.0-4.7). How RRs were derived from a logit model is not stated.
rows.evidence: jama_zahid pp1,3,6 (text); joi250093supp2 pp12-14 (rendered at 110 dpi and read). Recalculation r/p20765.R. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: A logistic model yields odds ratios; the report labels its estimates RR and 'crude' without describing a conversion. Values labeled crude RR cannot be crude risk ratios (TB success 1.2 when the arm risks give 1.04; 1.1 when the risks are identical). The headline RR 3.0 (abstract) is therefore of unclear estimand: it is neither the crude RR (2.73) nor the crude OR (3.96). Confirmed reporting issue; substantive because the primary effect estimate in the abstract is affected; J direct.

rows.R: SAP §36 p92 (OCR): fully adjusted model includes tobacco use form plus baseline characteristics (education, smoking duration). Article p3/p4 and Table 2 footnote a: adjusted RR 3.2 adjusted for age, sex, education, occupation, smoking duration, 'selected post hoc'; no tobacco-use-form term (despite smokeless use 6.9% vs 2.2% imbalance). Disclosed as post hoc covariate selection.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 p92 (OCR); jama_zahid pp3-4,6; joi250093supp2 p14. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The planned adjusted primary model differs from the reported one; the report discloses that covariates were chosen post hoc but does not report the planned tobacco-form adjustment. Disclosed; retained per the fixed decision. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SAP p84 primary: CO <10 ppm. Article p3-4: CO <6 ppm is a post hoc sensitivity analysis (disclosed). Table 2 p6 and eTable 9 p13 list the CO<6 ITT and PP rows inside the 'Primary outcome' block. The analysis is unplanned and disclosed; the table heading groups it with the primary outcome, which a reader can resolve from the text. Disclosed.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 p84 (OCR); jama_zahid pp3-4,6; joi250093supp2 p13. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: A disclosed post hoc analysis is still a plan-report difference under the fixed decision, so retained; the status mislabel itself is presentational because the text states it is post hoc. L minor_presentation.

rows.R: Protocol v4.0 p28 and v6.0 p66 (OCR): outcomes 'primarily analysed in a missing-at-random architecture' with GLMMs. SAP p91 and article p3: ITT with all missing primary outcomes counted as smoking (Russell Standard), plus complete-case analysis. 95/1080 (8.8%) missing, including 52 deaths.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp28,66,91 (OCR); jama_zahid pp3-4. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Missing-data assumption for the primary analysis changes from MAR to deterministic nonabstinence. With differential deaths (25/720 vs 27/360), the choice affects arm-specific denominators. The report's rule is conventional for cessation trials and matches the SAP, but differs from the protocol. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SAP §38 pp92-93 and shell p99 (OCR): subgroups include gender (male vs female). Article p3 lists prespecified subgroups age, education, employment, smoking duration; eTable 8 p12 has no gender row (but adds 'Reading SMS'). No gender subgroup result anywhere. Only 37 women enrolled, which may explain omission, but no reason is given.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp92-93,99 (OCR); jama_zahid pp3,5; joi250093supp2 p12 (rendered). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: A planned subgroup analysis is unreported and the report's list of 'prespecified' subgroups omits it. L substantive_difference (planned analysis not reported).

rows.R: Protocol v6.0 p48 and p62 (OCR) state 10% missing primary data for the whole multi-phase study (2,716 participants), but the Phase 3 calculation in the same protocol (p63) uses 20% attrition (587 to 704), as do the SAP (p83) and the article (p3). For Phase 3, plan and report agree; the 10% is a stale overall figure inside the plan (2,716 = 1080 + 1620 + 16 is itself built from 20%-inflated phase totals).
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp48,62-64,77,83 (OCR); jama_zahid p3.
rows.rationale: The plan's Phase 3 sample-size derivation and the report both assume 20% attrition, so no plan-report difference exists for the trial reported. The 10% statement is a plan-internal inconsistency in the overall multi-phase summary, not a design element of this analysis. Excluded. Separately noted: the protocol computes 704 x 1.5 = '~1080', but 704 x 1.5 = 1056.

rows.R: E changed to statistical_results (numerical misattribution). Discussion p8: '4.8% of the trial participants died of TB within 6 months'. Deaths from all causes were 52/1080 = 4.8%; TB deaths were 32/1080 = 3.0% (eTable 4 p6: 32 TB deaths; article p5: 61.5% [32/52]). The all-cause figure is presented as TB-specific mortality and used to compare with a prior trial.
rows.evidence: jama_zahid pp1,4-6,8; joi250093supp2 p6 (rendered). Recalculation r/p20765.R.
rows.rationale: 32/1080 = 2.96%; 52/1080 = 4.81%. The statement overstates TB mortality by about 60% and underpins the comparison with an earlier trial. Tables give the correct counts, but the narrative figure is wrong. I classify this as a numerical reporting error (statistical_results) rather than a report-internal inconsistency, consistent with the Codebook's instruction for numerical errors. Confirmed; substantive for interpretation of mortality; J possible.

rows.R: Article p5 lists any-symptom prevalences irritability 40.5% vs 43.4% and anxiety 33.3% vs 36.8% (mHealth vs usual care), then says 'dry mouth, irritability, and anxiety were more common in the mHealth group'. For irritability and anxiety any-symptom prevalence is lower with mHealth; eTable 10 p15 shows the significant chi-square reflects more moderate/severe grades (irritability 15.5% vs 8.4%; anxiety 9.3% vs 3.9%). Epigastric pain differed significantly in the other direction and is not mentioned.
rows.evidence: jama_zahid p5; joi250093supp2 p15 (rendered at 110 dpi). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The narrative contradicts its own percentages for 'more common'; the accurate statement is that moderate/severe grades were more common. Confirmed; minor because the severity shift is real and the table is clear; J unlikely.

rows.R: Ratio estimates vs geometric midpoint of their CIs (r/p20765.R): some rows are log-symmetric (eTable 8 age <40: 2.672 vs 2.674; Table 2 self-report crude 2.7 vs 2.72), many are not (eTable 8 All 2.890 vs 3.056; age >=40 2.953 vs 3.229; dependent 2.587 vs 2.302; eTable 9 CO<10 crude 2.9 vs 3.39; Table 2 CO<6 PP adjusted 3.8 vs 4.21). Asymmetric intervals can arise from legitimate methods (e.g., converted OR intervals, profile likelihood), and the interval method is not stated, so inconsistency cannot be established. Also noted: Table 2 self-report adjusted CI printed '1.9 to 42' (typo for 4.2).
rows.evidence: jama_zahid p6; joi250093supp2 pp12-14 (rendered). Recalculation r/p20765.R. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Within the same displays, which use one stated method, some intervals are symmetric on the log scale and others are skewed in different directions (estimate both below and above the geometric midpoint), which is unusual for a single method. Without the interval method I cannot decide whether rows are wrong; related to C006 (undefined RR derivation). Indeterminate; J possible since these are extractable subgroup and sensitivity estimates.

rows.R: Treatment failure: protocol v4.0 p9 = smear-positive at month 5 or later; protocol v6.0 (latest) p47 = month 6 or later; change log p77 records the 5 to 6 correction; SAP p85 (which cites protocol v6.0) = month 5. The latest protocol and the SAP define the secondary outcome differently. Also, the v4.0 pages carry a running header 'V6.0 07.03.25', which confuses version identification. Report (1/720 vs 2/360) does not state which definition was used.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp1 (TOC), 9, 47, 77, 85 (OCR at 300 dpi; overview render of pp1,42,43,46,76,78 to identify document boundaries). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The two current plan documents give different time windows for the treatment-failure outcome; month-5 positives count as failures under one and not the other. Event numbers are small, but it is an outcome definition conflict that a reader cannot resolve. K substantive_inconsistency.

rows.R: Protocol v6.0: overview p48 and Phase 3 calculation p63 use 18 intervention vs 9 control clusters; the repeated power paragraph p65 still says 16 vs 8 (and 20 per arm for Phase 4 vs 18 at p64); the change log p77 says v6 increased from 16+8 to 18+9; SAP p83 uses 27 clusters 2:1. Stale paragraph; the operative design (18:9) is clear.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp1 pp48,63-65,77,83 (OCR). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Real internal inconsistency in the latest protocol, but the amendment log, detailed calculation, SAP and report all agree on 18:9, so the intended design is unambiguous. K minor_presentation. Noted: the protocol's own arithmetic 704 x 1.5 is given as about 1080 (actual 1056).

rows.R: eTable 4 p6 (rendered): usual-care column 'Drug user 1 (7.4%)' and 'Severe pneumonia 1 (7.4%)'; 1/27 = 3.7%, as printed for 'History of fall' 1 (3.7%) in the same column. Overall column also has small slips: cancer 3/52 printed 5.7% (5.8%), heart attack 8/52 printed 15.2% (15.4%).
rows.evidence: joi250093supp2 p6 (rendered at 110 dpi). Recalculation r/p20765.R.
rows.rationale: 1/27 = 3.70%. Counts sum correctly (27 and 25), so only percentages are wrong. Confirmed; minor; J unlikely.

rows.R: eTable 6 p9 (rendered): control site 2008 deaths '5 (7.5)'; every cluster has 40 participants (eTable 5 p8), so 5/40 = 12.5% (7.5% = 3/40). Control deaths sum to 27 only with 5, so the count is right and the percentage wrong.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp2 pp8-9 (rendered). Recalculation r/p20765.R. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Control deaths 1+0+4+2+2+3+4+5+6 = 27 (matches Table 2); 5/40 = 12.5%. Confirmed; minor; J unlikely.

rows.R: eTable 9 p13: treatment failures 1/695 (0.1%) vs 2/333 (0.6%), absolute difference printed 0.5 (-0.4 to 1.3); other rows are mHealth minus usual care (e.g., 43.2 - 16.5 = 26.7), so this should be about -0.5. Same reversal in main Table 2 p6: death 3.5 vs 7.5 printed '4 (1.0 to 7.1)' and treatment failure 0.1 vs 0.5 printed '0.4 (-0.4 to 1.2)'.
rows.evidence: joi250093supp2 pp13-14 (rendered); jama_zahid p6. Recalculation: 100 x (1/695 - 2/333) = -0.46. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Sign convention is inconsistent within the tables; for rows where mHealth is lower the absolute differences are printed as positive. Direction is recoverable from the arm percentages. Confirmed; minor; J possible because an extractor taking the difference column would get the wrong sign (also for the mortality difference).

rows.R: Protocol v1.0 (Dec 2020) synopsis p7, endpoints p24, analysis p27 (OCR; text layer encoded): primary = comparative difference in mean total SOFA to day 9, Welch t-test; deaths use mean SOFA until death. SAP v2.0 (18 May 2024) pp66-67 and article p3/p6: responder endpoint (>=1.4-point decrease), Fisher exact test, deaths imputed as SOFA 24. Report follows the SAP, which is dated after last follow-up (29 Apr 2024, article p6).
rows.evidence: joi250116supp1 pp7,24-27,63,66-69 (OCR at 300 dpi); jama_giamarellosbourboulis pp3,5-6. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: The primary endpoint changed from a continuous mean difference to a dichotomized responder proportion, with a different test and a different rule for deaths (mean-to-death vs worst-score imputation). The governing SAP was finalized about three weeks after the last patient's follow-up; the report states that analyses followed the SAP but does not describe the change from the protocol. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SAP p66: last SOFA carried forward for patients 'discharged home' before day 9 (and lost to follow-up). Article p5 restates the home-discharge rule, but p6 says 8.3% had scores carried forward 'because of ICU discharge earlier than day 9' (eTable 8), and the sensitivity analysis excludes patients discharged before day 9. Applied trigger (ICU discharge) differs from the planned and stated trigger (home discharge).
rows.evidence: joi250116supp1 p66 (OCR); jama_giamarellosbourboulis pp3,5-6; joi250116supp2 pp20,46. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: SOFA was recorded daily during ICU stay only, so ICU discharge may be the practical point at which values stop; the plan does not say what happens to ward patients, and the report applies LOCF at ICU discharge while describing a home-discharge rule. Whether this is a deviation or an operational clarification cannot be decided from the documents; the report is also internally inconsistent. L indeterminate.

rows.R: Protocol p25: infection resolution and omics biomarkers are exploratory endpoints (synopsis p7 lists the omics under secondary). SAP pp68-70 lists infection resolution among secondary analyses; article p5 counts infection resolution by day 15 as the sixth prespecified secondary endpoint and reports it in Table 2 (OR 0.59, P=.02); omics endpoints are not mentioned. Outcome-status change relative to the protocol.
rows.evidence: joi250116supp1 pp7,25,27,57,70 (OCR); jama_giamarellosbourboulis pp5-7. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: An exploratory protocol endpoint is reported as a prespecified secondary endpoint, based on an SAP finalized after follow-up ended; it is one of the nominally significant secondary results. Omics endpoints planned in the protocol are not reported (planned for separate publication is plausible but not stated). L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol p25 and SAP pp69-70: reversal of immune dysfunction censored at day 15; MALS = ferritin decrease >=15% by day 15; immunoparalysis = HLA-DR >8000 (protocol also ferritin <4420); deaths count as non-reversal. Article p5-7, Table 2 footnote b: reversal 'by day 28', must persist over subsequent draws, >=2 serial draws required, evaluated in a subset of 125 patients (59 vs 66).
rows.evidence: joi250116supp1 pp25,69-70 (OCR); jama_giamarellosbourboulis pp5-7; joi250116supp2 p50. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Time window (15 vs 28 days), persistence/serial-draw requirement and analysis population (subset with blood sampling vs all patients with deaths as failures) all differ. These change the estimand of a reported significant secondary endpoint (78.0% vs 48.5%). L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol pp25-26 (OCR): power for a 1.4-point difference in mean SOFA, SD 3.2, two-sided t-test, 90% power. Article p5: powered for responder proportions 40% vs 20%, 117 per group, 280 with 15% dropout. The SAP (pp63-72) contains no binary power calculation. Recomputed: t-test 1.4/3.2 at 90% gives 111 per group; two proportions 40% vs 20% gives 108 per group (power.prop.test, no continuity correction).
rows.evidence: joi250116supp1 pp7,25-26,63-72 (OCR); jama_giamarellosbourboulis p5. R: power.t.test and power.prop.test.
rows.rationale: The sample-size basis reported in the article does not appear in any supplied plan; the planned basis was a continuous outcome. This accompanies the change of primary endpoint in C001. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol p27 and SAP p70: infection resolution analyzed as binary (resolved vs not) by Fisher exact test with Mantel-Haenszel OR, also by infection type and immune stratum. Article p6-7: 4-category ordinal regression (resolved, intermediate, failure, superinfection), OR 0.59 (0.38-0.91) for worse outcome, while p6 says all secondary end points were compared by Fisher exact test and all analyses followed the SAP.
rows.evidence: joi250116supp1 pp27,70 (OCR); jama_giamarellosbourboulis pp6-7; joi250116supp2 p49. Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Planned binary comparison not reported; an ordinal model is used instead, and the report's statement that it followed the SAP is not accurate for this endpoint. Binary resolution 58/131 vs 46/145 is shown in Table 2 without the planned test. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: SAP pp67-72 (OCR): Breslow-Day/Tarone homogeneity tests across immune states and severity subgroups; survivor-only mean SOFA t-tests by immune state (days 9 and 15); 28- and 90-day mortality by immune state; separate primary-endpoint analysis by appropriate vs inappropriate antibiotics. None found in the article or the 54-page supplement (searched for Breslow, Tarone, survivors, appropriate antibiotics; checked eTable/eFigure list).
rows.evidence: joi250116supp1 pp67-72 (OCR); jama_giamarellosbourboulis pp5-8; joi250116supp2 (full text search and contents list pp1-2). Card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Several planned analyses of the primary and key secondary endpoints are absent. eTable 10 gives per-stratum responder results but no homogeneity test; severity subgroups are shown with interaction terms rather than the planned Breslow-Day tests. L substantive_difference.

rows.R: eTable 10 p22: day-15 immunoparalysis 40/106 vs 29/122, OR printed 1.194 (1.09 to 3.45). Crude OR = (40/66)/(29/93) = 1.94 (Fisher conditional 1.94); geometric midpoint of the printed CI = 1.94. Transposed digits (1.944 printed as 1.194); the printed point lies at the edge of its own CI.
rows.evidence: joi250116supp2 p22 (text). Recalculation r/p24175.R.
rows.rationale: Counts, CI and P (.030) all fit OR 1.94. Confirmed typographic error in a subgroup secondary estimate; minor because the counts and CI expose the correct value; J possible (an extractor could take 1.194).

rows.R: eTable 13 p27: MALS any serious TEAE 20/25 (80.0%) anakinra vs 21/23 (91.3%) placebo. eTable 15 p44 reports 'number needed to treat to induce at least 1 serious TEAE (NNH1)' = 8.8 (3.2 to 10.0). Risk is lower with anakinra: RD -11.3 points, 1/RD = -8.8, i.e., a number needed to benefit, not to harm.
rows.evidence: joi250116supp2 pp27,29,44 (rendered at 120 dpi). Recalculation r/p24175.R.
rows.rationale: The magnitude 8.8 = 1/0.113 matches, but its direction is reversed: the table presents a harm metric where the intervention had fewer events. In a benefit-risk table this misstates the safety direction for the anakinra stratum. Confirmed; substantive for interpretation of the benefit-risk summary; J possible.
